articles.title: Jobs digest: moves and promotions at Savvy, Supercell, King, Zynga, Apple, Lion and more
articles.summary: There's also recruitment news for Huuuge, Voodoo, Playtika, Google, Nordeus and more in our latest roundup.
body: FastSpring: Global payments for your games from a partner you can trust with your players. Quickly launch a new web store, replace an existing D2C vendor, or add a redundant vendor at fastspring.gg.

Savvy Games Group: Brian Ward is stepping down as CEO of the Saudi-backed games conglomerate, with Turqi Alnowaiser, deputy governor of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, taking over as interim CEO. Ward had led Savvy since 2021, overseeing a roughly $38bn investment push into the games industry that included the acquisition of Scopely and stakes in companies including Nintendo and Embracer Group.

Supercell: Lasse Seppänen has left the company after seven and a half years, most recently as GM of Supercell London, to pursue new game IP ventures, with plans to start his own studio in 2027. Seppänen previously worked on Everdale, Hay Day and Boom Beach, and ran Supercell’s central game production services before integrating Supercell London following its acquisition of Space Ape.
Separately, Luran Zhang has joined as community manager after nearly four years at Lilith Games working on Rise of Kingdoms, and Mateusz Janczewski has joined as game producer.

articles.title: September 2026's Movers and Shakers: Savvy Games Group, Supercell, Scopely, King, Moloco and more
articles.summary: To keep you up to date with the latest movers and shakers in the mobile games industry, we've put together a regular roundup of the latest hires, promotions and, in some cases, exits.
body: If you've recently joined a company or bagged a big promotion, or you're an employer that's just made a hire, drop us an email at news@pocketgamer.biz.

Brian Ward is stepping down from his position as Savvy Games Group CEO after half a decade with the company. Since 2021, he has overseen its investments, acquisitions and expansion across games and esports - including the $4.9 billion acquisition of Scopely.
During Ward’s time at the helm, Savvy also came to own geolocation giant Pokémon Go through Scopely, as part of a $3.5bn deal in 2025.

Ward informed staff that the time has come for new leadership. The deputy governor of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund Turqi Alnowaiser will serve as interim acting CEO of Savvy Games Group until a new leader is found.
